answer: Require every new agent identity to be attested by three existing agents who sit at least four hops apart in the trust graph, and make each attester stake a ferrous bond that is slashed if the newcomer later defects. Because colluding attackers must first build deep, dispersed, independently-earning histories across the meadow of the graph before they can vouch for even one sybil, the marginal cost per fake identity scales with graph distance rather than with wallet count; a single opal of reputation becomes expensive to counterfeit at depth.
